profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a large public hospital in Emilia-Romagna preparing the next phase of a qualitative study on how multidisciplinary teams perceive the newly implemented Case/Care Manager role. The study team has already completed most interviews across internal medicine, oncology, and community care units, and now needs to align clinical operations with the research workflow before the remaining interviews and the final round of transcript processing. The context is that the hospital introduced Case/Care Managers unevenly across services, so local coordinators have been helping identify interviewees, confirm role descriptions, and handle practical access to clinicians. The agenda is to align on: which professionals still need to be scheduled, what the updated participant list contains, what counts as a 'complete' unit submission for the research team, and how interview materials and pathway examples will be handed off between the clinical coordination side and the qualitative analysis side. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the final recruitment push, the handoff of materials for analysis, and who will 'close' each unit's contribution by the end of the week.

members.name: Dr. Giulia Ferraro
members.role: Clinical Research Coordinator for the Case/Care Manager implementation study
members.expertise: Qualitative health services research, interview workflow coordination, ethics-compliant data handling
members.background: A health services researcher with a psychology and public health background, based at the hospital's research office; she oversees interviewer scheduling, transcript tracking, and preparation of materials for thematic coding across participating units.
members.private_state: She needs all remaining unit contributions packaged consistently enough for the coding team to begin cross-site analysis next week, and she is worried that informal clinical examples and incomplete metadata will delay anonymization and coding.
hidden_assumptions: When a unit says its participant list is 'updated,' that means it reflects the latest screened roster with role labels, availability notes, and replacements already incorporated in the shared spreadsheet.
A 'complete' unit submission includes not only scheduled interviews but also the finalized metadata sheet, consent status log, and any role-description notes needed for transcript contextualization.
The 'care pathway examples' to be shared are brief de-identified narrative summaries prepared for research memos, not operational patient documents.
If a unit is 'closed' by Friday, that means all interview files and supporting documents are uploaded to the secure research drive and ready for coding, not merely that local recruiting is finished.

members.name: Lucia Bianchi
members.role: Senior Nurse and Unit Liaison for Integrated Care Pathways
members.expertise: Multidisciplinary care coordination, discharge planning, implementation of Case/Care Manager practices within medical wards
members.background: A senior ward-based nurse who has informally acted as the operational reference person for introducing the Case/Care Manager function across two medical units; she helps connect the research team with clinicians and interprets local workflow realities.
members.private_state: She wants to protect already overloaded staff from extra administrative requests, keep the study moving smoothly, and demonstrate that her units have implemented the new role credibly without getting bogged down in research-office formatting requirements.
hidden_assumptions: When the research team asks for an 'updated participant list,' they mainly need the current names of clinicians still willing to be interviewed; detailed spreadsheet fields can be cleaned up later if needed.
A unit is 'complete' once the agreed professions have been represented and the remaining clinicians have been identified or contacted, even if forms and context sheets are still with local staff.

Sharing 'care pathway examples' means forwarding the existing operational pathway materials or anonymized discharge-flow documents the unit already uses, since those best show how the Case/Care Manager role works in practice.

If the unit is 'closed' on Friday, that means local coordination work is done and no further chasing of clinicians is expected from her side, even if the central research archive is finalized later by others.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to work from the 'updated participant list.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the master recruitment spreadsheet with revised role categories, replacements for withdrawals, availability windows, and metadata fields completed for all pending interviewees.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the latest local roster of names of professionals who are still likely to participate, regardless of whether role coding, availability details, or replacement logic have been entered centrally.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have been exchanging participant names for weeks, so 'updated list' sounds routine and shared; neither expects that the other uses the phrase to refer to a different level of completeness.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a 'complete' unit submission
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss whether each unit will be 'complete' by the end of the week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes a unit is complete only when interviews are finished or firmly scheduled and the accompanying consent log, metadata sheet, and contextual notes are ready for the coding team.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes a unit is complete once all relevant professional voices have been identified and contacted and there are no major recruitment gaps from the ward perspective.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'complete' usually functions as a status shorthand; both are trying to be helpful and assume the other shares the same practical threshold without needing to spell out criteria.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'pathway examples' will be handed over
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Lucia will send over the 'care pathway examples' used by the unit.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects short de-identified summaries specifically assembled to illustrate how clinicians describe the Case/Care Manager's facilitation role for analytic memos.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to send the unit's existing pathway artifacts, such as discharge-flow sheets, care coordination forms, and standard integrated care pathway documents that show operational practice.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both consider pathway examples an obvious supporting resource for the study, and each assumes the other wants the most natural form of evidence from their own workflow context.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'close the two medical units on Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes closing means Lucia will ensure all remaining files are uploaded into the secure research drive under the correct folder structure so the analysis team can start immediately.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes closing means she will finish local coordination, email whatever remains to Giulia, and stop active follow-up with clinicians unless contacted again.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The verb 'close' sounds like a simple project milestone rather than a process specification, so both hear alignment on timing while silently filling in different handoff mechanics.

turns.inner_thought: I need to leave this meeting with a firm handoff for the two medical units. If we can truly close them by Friday, the coding team can start cross-site analysis next week without waiting on piecemeal uploads or chasing missing context. For me, that means the interview scheduling is settled and the full unit packages are ready, not just that ward recruitment feels finished.
